newsitem.title: CHINA: Shanghai seen helping Hong Kong after handover.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai seen helping Hong Kong after handover.

text.p: Shanghai will not attempt to undermine Hong Kong's role as an international financial centre after the British colony reverts to Chinese rule, a senior central bank official said.

The China Daily Business Weekly, in its Sunday edition, quoted Mao Yinglian, head of the Shanghai branch of the People's Bank of China, as saying China could support two financial centres after the handover.
"Hong Kong will benefit from a partnership with Shanghai, particularly in involvement with mainland projects," Mao said.
Hong Kong will revert to Beijing's sovereignty at midnight on June 30, 1997, becoming a Special Administrative Region of China.
Mao said Shanghai can serve as a stepping stone for Hong Kong investment into inland China, as well as offering opportunites in the areas of foreign exchange, interbank loans and securities.
Some analysts believe China's central government support for Shanghai and high growth rates may eventually see the city surpass Hong Kong as a financial centre.
